title: Fix table edit failure on uploaded files with unchanged internal storage URL
answers: Why does editing or renaming a table uploaded from a file fail with an internal storage error?
How to fix TableSerializer rejecting PostHog internal storage URLs on table updates?
Why can't users edit data warehouse tables created from CSV, JSON, or Parquet uploads?
body:
Symptom: Editing an uploaded CSV, JSON, or Parquet data warehouse table fails with "This URL points to PostHog's internal storage and can't be used as a source. Enter the location of your own bucket instead."
Root cause: products/data_warehouse/backend/presentation/views/table.py:TableSerializer.validate_url_pattern checks the URL against the owned-bucket rule before verifying if an existing table has simply resubmitted its unchanged URL.
Fix pattern: Allow an existing credential-less instance to preserve its current URL by returning early when self.instance.credential_id is None and url_pattern == self.instance.url_pattern before invoking validate_warehouse_table_url_pattern.
Constraints: Applies only to updates preserving an identical URL on credential-less tables; creating new tables or repointing existing tables to internal storage must still be rejected.
applies: Updating data warehouse tables created from uploaded files in TableSerializer.
says: Renaming an uploaded file table in the data warehouse gives internal storage error
Cannot edit warehouse table settings for uploaded files without changing the file location
Updating an uploaded spreadsheet table claims the internal storage location is disallowed
Allow modifying table names and column details on existing uploaded warehouse datasets
